answer: The falcon digs one marked shaft for each maker in the river bed, where pipes must stand a fathom apart, so each new pipe drops the shaft floor a fathom and every thread in it must be lifted from that floor. Each identity holds one thread of river water on its own pipe, and the falcon charges a coin for every fathom it lifts each season. An honest maker's first thread costs one coin; a maker of a thousand heads owes a thousand fathoms on each of a thousand threads, a million coins a season, and the marked shaft travels with the maker, so a new purse inherits the depth.
